newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian army reports large cocaine seizure.
newsitem.headline: Colombian army reports large cocaine seizure.

text.p: The Colombian army said on Thursday it had seized more than 13,000 pounds (6,000 kg) of cocaine -- one of the year's biggest drug hauls -- in a raid on a clandestine drug laboratory run by leftist guerrillas.

An army spokesman said the raid took place in the jungle-covered southern province of Caqueta. The lab, overflowing with cocaine and precursor chemicals used to process the drug from coca leaves, belonged to rebels of the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC), the spokesman said.

The FARC, Colombia's largest and oldest guerrilla group, has long been known to provide protection for rural drug farms and laboratories. But government and military officials say it has now branched out into drug processing and trafficking and become a communist-led cartel.
The drug haul in Caqueta brought the total amount of cocaine either seized or destroyed by Colombia's armed forces so far this year to more than 35 tons (almost 32 tonnes).
